meta.title: Hive · browser task to CLI worker
meta.subtitle: Local PTY-based team path · task plans are not dispatches · source snapshot f8f1343

components.label: Browser workbench
components.explanation: The browser saves task Markdown over HTTP and subscribes to task snapshots. User goals can be submitted to the orchestrator through the user-input API; interactive terminal input and output use WebSockets. This is a UI, not the runtime that executes the CLI agents.

components.label: PTY host + terminal hub
components.explanation: AgentManager launches real CLI processes through node-pty in a configured working directory. The runtime owns their PTYs; xterm in the browser is a viewer/controller. The terminal hub subscribes to the PTY output bus and sends output to viewers, with restore and flow control. The user-input HTTP route requires a UI session and an active orchestrator, then delivers its prompt. Team delivery arrows elsewhere represent the stdin adapter writing these same owned PTYs, not a second process transport.

components.label: Orchestrator CLI
components.explanation: The orchestrator is itself a CLI agent, not a scheduler inside the browser. It can query runnable tasks with team next, choose a member and invoke team send. It reads recorded collaboration via team messages. Final reports are injected as incoming messages. Which task it chooses, what it implements, and the correctness of its synthesis depend on the CLI agent; this source implements transport and bookkeeping, not a deterministic planner.

components.label: .hive/tasks.md
components.explanation: Task routes read and atomically write this workspace file through TasksFileService. A watcher reads changed bytes and emits updated content; the tasks WebSocket publishes snapshots back to the browser. team next is a planning query over this file. Saving this file does not dispatch a worker, and accepting team report does not automatically mark a Markdown checkbox complete.

components.label: Worker CLI
components.explanation: Receives a dispatch envelope containing dispatch_id, task text and required_seen_seq in PTY stdin. The worker invokes the team helper as a CLI subprocess, using HIVE_PORT, HIVE_PROJECT_ID, HIVE_AGENT_ID and HIVE_AGENT_TOKEN to call the loopback HTTP API. Task progress uses team message --kind progress --to orchestrator; completion uses team report with the dispatch and any required seen sequence. Artifact arguments are path references, not an artifact-byte upload in this command.

components.label: Team API + delivery
components.explanation: The team routes authenticate agent tokens, workspace membership and role capabilities. Team operations persist a dispatch, claim it, and use the stdin dispatcher to paste/submit the task envelope. A stopped user-managed worker keeps a queued dispatch until started; a newly spawned, never-started worker may be auto-started. Reports require a reportable open dispatch and the current required seen sequence. The report and durable outbox entry are committed together, then delivery to the orchestrator is attempted. Progress is stored, not pushed into its PTY. HTTP 202 is acceptance, not proof that the agent has acted.

sources.label: Commit report then deliver or queue

components.label: Runtime SQLite
components.explanation: These stores share the runtime database. Dispatch state progresses from queued to submitted to reported (or cancelled). Progress messages get no delivery-outbox entry. The report mutation checks the owner's required inbound non-progress message sequence before writing report text and artifact paths. The report outbox is marked delivered only after the PTY write resolves; that still does not prove the orchestrator understood the result.

cards.title: 1 · Plan is not dispatch
items: User goal → orchestrator CLI → team send → worker stdin.
Task Markdown is a separate plan; team next queries runnable items.
No automatic tasks.md → worker scheduler is established here.

cards.title: 2 · Progress is not completion
items: team message --kind progress records an update without waking the orchestrator.
Read it through team messages or UI message history; terminal output is also live.
team report closes the dispatch only after the current seen-sequence gate passes.

cards.title: 3 · Durable result, bounded guarantee
items: Report text + artifact paths + outbox entry commit before PTY forwarding.
If the orchestrator is down, the report waits; team list after restart drains it.
PTY write success is not proof of agent understanding, task success or checkbox completion.

cards.title: Scope & boundaries
items: Browser is only the UI; both agents are local CLI child processes with owned PTYs.
Terminal host and team control are cooperating subsystems of one Node runtime.
UI session vs agent token + workspace + role checks are distinct authorization boundaries.
Local orchestrator path only: remote gateway, external controllers and workflow runner omitted.
